classification: Actual automation CLI extra-agent-args behavior with controlled runtime ports
rationale: Read every declaration, parameter row, helper and fixture. Preserve all distinct parser/routing/output controls. Strengthen public error envelopes and actual dispatch/latch boundaries; restore process exit status in failure-safe teardown. No native app, shell, provider or remote host is launched.

cases.title: sends the exact text after confirming the runtime applies it
cases.reason: Confirm exactly status.get, owner read and update, preserving the complete quoted extra-args text. These are the actual CLI dispatch arguments, not echoed mock-call assertions without a transformation.

cases.title: clears with an explicit empty value without a capability probe
cases.reason: An explicit empty string must reach the real edit dispatch after the owner read with exactly two calls; no capability probe or extra dispatch may occur.

cases.title: refuses nonempty extras on a runtime that would drop them
cases.reason: An old host lacking capability must produce a single structured incompatible_runtime error and exit 1 after status.get only. Preserve independent upgrade text and restore exitCode even when an assertion fails.

cases.title: passes positional automation ids to edit, remove, run, and show
cases.reason: Exercise all four public positional commands, retaining seven ordered owner/write/read calls and the complete disabled edit shape. This protects parser-to-handler integration beyond isolated flag tests.

cases.title: rejects ambiguous positional and flag automation ids before dispatch
cases.reason: Conflicting positional/flag IDs must emit one structured invalid_argument and exit 1 before any dispatch. Move exitCode restoration into failure-safe suite teardown.

classification: Actual automation CLI run-output behavior with controlled runtime ports
rationale: Read every declaration, parameter row, helper and fixture. Preserve all distinct parser/routing/output controls. Strengthen public error envelopes and actual dispatch/latch boundaries; restore process exit status in failure-safe teardown. No native app, shell, provider or remote host is launched.

cases.title: prints the authoritative $status outcome without unknown handles
cases.reason: All nine independent host statuses retain their exact human acknowledgements, exact full IDs, scheduled timestamp and absence of invented workspace handles. Verify the actual runNow request after owner read.

cases.title: prints workspace and terminal identities only when supplied by the host
cases.reason: The formatter must include the exact host-supplied folder workspace, terminal session, pane and PTY identities; the real CLI formatter rather than the fixture producer generates the output.

cases.title: preserves the supplied precheck and error on a skipped run
cases.reason: Skipped precheck output must retain its actual exit-1 diagnostic and the separate run failure instead of claiming a launched run.

cases.title: adds a JSON runId while retaining the %s run and RPC metadata
cases.reason: All five JSON status rows preserve the full host run and RPC envelope while adding runId. This exercises a real CLI output transformation and protects the machine-readable result contract.

cases.title: prints no acknowledgment until the host returns a delayed result
cases.reason: Replace polling and a default no-op responder with explicit request/response latches. Hold the actual runNow result, require zero acknowledgement before release, then release and await in finally and verify the sole started acknowledgement.

cases.title: supports old host responses that omit terminal identity fields
cases.reason: A legacy run omitting optional pane/PTY fields must remain intact in JSON with runId and envelope; compatibility fields must not be invented.

cases.title: prints an unfamiliar newer-host status without claiming the run started
cases.reason: An unfamiliar future host status must be printed literally in the generic acknowledgement without claiming it started.

cases.title: preserves the SSH owner fence while adding the runId
cases.reason: The owner precondition returned by show must survive into runNow while adding the public JSON runId. This protects SSH generation fencing through the actual command route.

cases.title: preserves the %s environment in the follow-up command
cases.reason: Both explicit and ambient environment selection must keep the selected named host in follow-up argv; explicit selection must suppress wrong-host ambient state. Platform-specific quoting is checked without launching a shell.

cases.title: requires same-target guidance for the Windows shell-sensitive label %s
cases.reason: Keep all six independently chosen Windows expansion/metacharacter labels. Each must emit same-host/profile guidance instead of an unsafe re-executable label. Platform is stubbed, no native shell is launched.

cases.title: requires same-target guidance for a label that would parse as another flag
cases.reason: A leading -- environment must retain same-target guidance because copying it as a flag value would change parsing.

cases.title: quotes an expansion-sensitive environment literally for POSIX shells
cases.reason: POSIX $box is quoted literally with single quotes so follow-up guidance cannot expand the environment name. The actual quote formatter is exercised.

cases.title: requires the same target without exposing %s pairing credentials
cases.reason: Explicit and both ambient pairing credential paths must never expose the test credential in text, JSON or help. Retain each source and the same-target follow-up guidance.

cases.title: requires the same custom profile with environment selection %s
cases.reason: Both plain and named-environment custom profiles must require preserving connection/profile settings without exposing the private profile path; keep exactly two host calls.

cases.title: rejects the unsupported --user-data-dir flag before selecting a runtime
cases.reason: Unsupported --user-data-dir must fail with invalid_argument before selecting a runtime; existing finally already restores process exit status.

cases.title: explains full UUIDs and pending launch behavior in run help
cases.reason: Public run help must explain full UUIDs and pending/dispatching admission, include an actionable example and avoid RPC. This checks rendered CLI help, not source-string presence.

cases.title: rejects invalid automation --day values before calling the runtime

cases.title: rejects automation schedule modifier mismatch: $name
cases.reason: Retain all three preset/modifier incompatibilities with independently expected messages. Each actual public command must return structured invalid_argument and zero RPC before exit 1.

cases.title: rejects bare automation --time on $name
cases.reason: Retain both create and edit bare --time argv arrays. They must reach format validation and emit structured invalid_argument mentioning HH:MM before RPC; teardown restores exitCode on failure.

cases.title: rejects automation edit schedule modifiers without a schedule flag
cases.reason: An edit day without trigger/schedule must fail through the modifier-requires-schedule path with structured invalid_argument, exact guidance and zero RPC.

cases.title: rejects conflicting automation session reuse flags

cases.title: clears automation source context on edit with null

cases.title: rejects invalid automation source context JSON before calling the runtime
cases.reason: Malformed JSON must reach the source-context parser and return structured invalid_argument with valid-JSON guidance, exit 1 and no RPC; restore exitCode regardless of assertion outcome.

cases.title: creates an automation for the enclosing worktree by default
cases.reason: Default create must infer the enclosing Git worktree from nested cwd and dispatch exact workspace, self destination, schedule and original create fields. Mock replies supply host data; production chooses the target.

cases.title: resolves project and host flags for automation create
cases.reason: With local and GPU setups present, explicit project/runtime host must select repo-gpu, the remote client and the full exact run context. Preserve the local distractor to catch first-row selection.

cases.title: resolves project-host-setup flags for automation edit with explicit run context
cases.reason: Editing by setup ID must look up that setup and forward its exact project/host/repo/path context after owner and destination reads.

cases.title: rejects automation create with both repo and workspace targets
cases.reason: Create with both repo and workspace must fail with structured invalid_argument and independent either-target guidance before any RPC; preserve exit 1 with failure-safe teardown.

cases.title: rejects automation edit with both repo and workspace targets
cases.reason: Edit has a distinct explicit-target path; retain its contradictory-target command and require structured invalid_argument, exact guidance, exit 1 and zero RPC.

cases.title: rejects automation create --$flag with a string value
cases.reason: Both enabled and disabled string-value rows retain independent flags/messages. Each must reject as structured invalid_argument before RPC rather than treating false text as truthy.

cases.title: resolves explicit automation create workspace active from cwd
cases.reason: Explicit active create must resolve the nested cwd through the actual selector and send exact workspace/self destination and default daily schedule, not forward active literally.

cases.title: resolves explicit automation edit workspace current from cwd
cases.reason: Explicit current edit must infer the same workspace while retaining enabled=true and the full original update/destination shape. Create and edit travel separate target paths.
